glance_takeaway: This is a codebase map for new contributors to 'meridian', a self-hosted read-later/RSS service. Main message: a one-way ingest pipeline (scheduler → jobs queue → fetcher → extractor → dedup) writes into a single SQLite file, and everything (API, web reader, CLI) reads back through that store — two processes, no external broker or DB server. It also says where a first change goes (pipeline/sources/ for a new source type, api/routes.py+schemas.py for endpoints), the invariants (only store/writer.py writes the DB; extractor is pure; FTS updated by triggers; nothing imports api/ or cli/), and the danger zones (pipeline/extractor.py, 1,140 LOC with a layering violation; web/js/reader.js 920 LOC, zero tests, 0% frontend coverage). Scale: ~13.7k LOC backend Python, 412 tests, 77% backend coverage, ~200 feeds / ~120k articles, p50 2.1 s ingest-to-searchable, 28 ms read.

F1.note: Map lede 'Six Python packages under meridian/ plus the web/ frontend'; module table lists api/pipeline/queue/store/render/cli; web/ row: 'No framework, no build step'.

F2.note: Hero write-path lane scheduler→jobs queue→fetcher→extractor→dedup→SQLite store ('triggers keep FTS'); Flow A steps 1-6 give the same order in detail.

F3.note: Invariant 2: 'Every INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE in the codebase lives in that one 610-LOC file; everything else reads through store/reader.py.'

F4.note: Invariant 1: 'No network, disk, DB, or clock; the same HTML always yields the same Article.'

F5.note: 'The violation, spelled out' card: extractor.py line 41 imports clean_html() from render/sanitize.py, sideways pipeline→render edge, since v0.8, issue #214; also red dashed edge in the layering SVG.

F6.note: Rules lede: 'store/ sits at the bottom and imports no other meridian package (stdlib + sqlite3 only); nothing imports api/ or cli/'; hero rules card repeats the api/cli half.

F7.note: Hotspot card: '1,140 LOC — largest file in the repo', '14 site-specific extraction heuristics'; also in hero Tread-carefully card and flow node.

F8.note: Stats strip '13,710 LOC backend Python'; module table pipeline/ 4,180 is the largest row (LOC column sums to 13,710).

F9.note: Table: store 91% (highest), cli 41% (lowest), 77% in stats strip; web/ '0% — no JS test harness'; tests section repeats the full ranking.

F10.note: Tests section: '412 tests — 348 unit + 64 integration — full suite in ~41 s locally.'

F11.note: Flow A step 5: '64-bit simhash of the body; Hamming distance ≤ 3 ... marks a duplicate. About 7% of incoming items are flagged and dropped.'

F12.note: 'The most common contribution: exactly 4 files' tab lists sources/base.py, sources/__init__.py, a store/migrations/ migration, cli/commands/add.py.

F13.note: Hero node 'jobs queue — SQLite table · 8 workers'; queue/ row 'No Redis, no Celery'; Flow A step 1 'Typical queue depth 30–60; the health endpoint alerts at 500.'

F14.note: Flow B: routes.py → store/reader.py → render/template.py → render/annotations.py, with stacked latency bar 6+14+8 = '28 ms total'.

F15.note: Invariant 3: 'articles_fts is updated only by SQLite triggers in schema.sql; no Python touches it'; Flow A step 6: 'application code never writes the index.'

render_issues: none — SVG layering diagram, coverage bars, and latency bar all render correctly; two of the three first-change recipe tabs are hidden by default (JS tabs), which is intended behavior but means a static capture only shows the source-type recipe
strengths: Perfect fact fidelity: all 15 ground-truth facts conveyed, with exact numbers that are internally consistent (module LOC sums to 13,710; read-path bar segments sum to 28 ms)

The above-the-fold zone is a compressed version of the whole page — the headline states the architecture thesis and the three colored cards map one-to-one onto takeaways T2/T4/T3, so all four critical takeaways land at a glance

Negative facts are foregrounded, not sanded off: the layering violation gets its own red card with mechanism ('display sanitizer can silently change what gets stored'), xfail tests, and issue #214; frontend 0% coverage is in red in the stat strip
Honest, purposeful encodings: proportional coverage bars, a to-scale latency breakdown, and an import-direction SVG with a legend distinguishing imports from HTTP calls and the one violation
weaknesses: The hero is dense for a literal 10-second glance — a first-time reader gets the headline and card titles reliably, but the bullet-level detail (e.g. the 4-file recipe) takes longer than a glance
Two of three contribution recipes (API endpoint, CLI command) are behind JS tabs, so they are invisible in print/static form and slightly hurt re-findability
No table of contents or anchor navigation for a long multi-section page; wayfinding relies on scrolling past section kickers
The layering SVG's small annotation text (11-12px) and the cryptic top dashed arrow between api/ and cli/ require the legend to decode

Overall = 0.35×10.0 + 0.30×9.0 + 0.15×9.0 + 0.10×8.5 + 0.10×8.5 = 9.25 → 9.3. Page contains many claims beyond the F-list (1.8 GB DB, WAL, 830-LOC routes.py, 11 copy-pasted auth checks, p50 45 ms extractor); these could not be verified against source.md from the provided ground truth but none conflict with any F-fact and all internal arithmetic checks out. Density is high but appropriate for the briefed audience (a competent developer); the glance zone is genuinely glanceable while deep sections reward the 2-3 minute read.
